advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a negative-control contract row exercising an adapter-bound internal (source/return_alias/_creation_channel/repo_root) and assert it produces no parity divergence.
evidence: Ticket AC: 'Adapter-bound internals (source/return_alias/_creation_channel/repo_root) produce no false divergence (negative-control row passes).'
Ticket Scope: 'Include a negative-control row over an adapter-bound internal (e.g. source) to confirm it is NOT flagged as a divergence.'
search_files for 'source'/'return_alias' in tests/interfaces/write_parity_contract.py returns no such row (only the module docstring line matches).
CASES list (write_parity_contract.py:111-207) contains create/transition/claim behavior rows only — no internal-param negative control.
advisory.finding: The contract table omits the AC-required negative-control row over an adapter-bound internal (source/return_alias/_creation_channel/repo_root) that must NOT register as a divergence. Without it, the oracle does not prove that transport-bound internals are correctly excluded from the parity surface.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a committed simulated-parity check that closes a gap in-suite and asserts the strict-xfail row now xpasses (the marker-removal forcing function).
evidence: Ticket AC: 'A committed, re-runnable simulated-parity check flips a strict-xfail row to xpass in-suite (not merely recorded as a ticket note), proving the oracle detects the fix.'
search_files for 'xpass'/'simulated' under tests/interfaces returns only docstring prose in the new files, no simulated-parity fixture/test.
The oracle (_params/test_write_parity) only records xfails; nothing simulates the gap closing to assert the xpass forcing-function fires.
advisory.finding: There is no committed, re-runnable in-suite check that flips a strict-xfail row to xpass to prove the oracle actually detects convergence (and would then force marker removal). The AC explicitly requires this as a test, not merely a ticket note.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document on the concurrency-wrong-current row that it must stay pre_in_progress=False (subject OPEN) so the fixed current='in_progress' is the deliberate mismatch.
evidence: Case(id="concurrency-wrong-current", op="transition", target="closed", inputs={}, expected=Result(REJECTED, code=10))
The only explanation is in execute(): 'the concurrency control leaves the subject OPEN so "in_progress" is deliberately the wrong current status' (write_parity_contract.py:254-257).
The row's correctness silently depends on pre_in_progress defaulting False AND the executor always passing current='in_progress'.
advisory.finding: The concurrency-control row relies on a non-obvious coupling — it leaves the subject OPEN (pre_in_progress omitted) so that the executor's hardcoded current='in_progress' is deliberately the wrong status — but the Case row carries no comment; the rationale lives only in the executor. A future edit adding pre_in_progress=True or changing the executor's fixed current would silently turn this negative control into a no-op without failing.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert store invariance on REJECTED rows (subject status unchanged from its pre-op state) so a rejection that silently mutates the ticket is caught.
evidence: tests/interfaces/test_write_parity_oracle.py:63: `if result.kind == ACCEPTED and case.expected_status and subject is not None:`

Rejection rows concurrency-wrong-current, close-class-missing-bug, reason-required-missing-bug expect Result(REJECTED, ...) with no expected_status, so no store state is read after the op (write_parity_contract.py:97-149).
ABSENCE: no assertion that a REJECTED op left the subject at its pre-op status; a partial/silent mutation accompanying a non-zero exit code would not be detected.
advisory.finding: REJECTED contract rows assert only the rejection classification/code, never that the store was left unmutated; a rejection that nonetheless applied a partial write (e.g. a param taking effect despite a non-zero exit) would still pass. The effect/store-invariance check in test_write_parity guards only ACCEPTED rows (`if result.kind == ACCEPTED and case.expected_status`), leaving the rejection side blind to a silent side-effect — the mirror of the very failure the ACCEPTED effect-check was written to catch.
scenarios: A future adapter or engine change applies a param (e.g. close_class or a status move) but still returns a rejection code — classification matches, but the ticket was silently mutated.
advisory.suggested_fix: Record the pre-op status in execute() (or re-derive the expected pre-op status per row) and, for REJECTED results, assert rebar.show_ticket(subject)['status'] equals that pre-op status.
